tracks.title: Descent into D Bayati
tracks.note: Made in Suno by the author on 2026-10-12 from the prompt below, written to match the desert's new procedural score (issue #207: src/score.js SCORES.desert, D bayati, 56 BPM); no song link was given. The MP3 as Suno gave it (2:45, 48 kHz, ~185 kb/s), not re-encoded. Replaces desert.mp3 (D hijaz, frame drum), retired in issue #207.
tracks.prompt: Style: ambient, mysterious, slow (56 BPM), D Bayati maqam. Solo oud, sparse and intimate, long held notes with slides like a fretless neck, plenty of silence between phrases. Under it: warm analog synth pads slowly opening, a low drone on D and A, soft desert wind, a faint granular shimmer, tape-style echoes panning left and right. Modern electronic textures for a sci-fi world of space exploration, but organic and human. No drums, no percussion loops, no vocals, no big build, no dramatic climax. Think Jon Hassell meets Anouar Brahem meets Hiroshi Yoshimura. Structure: instrumental, 2:30–3:00, seamless loop: drone swells in, oud states a falling motif (A–G–F–E half-flat–D), a gliding sine lead answers with a long theme (D–F–A–G–A), then the shimmer, the motif a step lower over a soft bass, thinning to one or two oud notes, then the drone alone back to the start. Exclude: drums, darbuka, frame drum, vocals, choir, strings swell, cinematic hits, EDM, trap.
tracks.direction: D bayati, 56 BPM, instrumental, no drums; solo oud with fretless slides, warm analog pads, a low D/A drone, desert wind, granular shimmer, tape echoes; ambient and mysterious

cues.title: Hiraeth - The Singing Light
cues.status: to record: the game sings the synth version until this file is here (docs/systems/audio.md, "The singing light's theme", has the Suno brief)
cues.direction: D lydian, 66 BPM, about 45 s, no drums; one wordless high voice (a soft 'oo', glass-like), a glass harmonica an octave over it, a very quiet low D drone swelling in threes; the five-note call A4, D5 E5, a glide up to G#5, a long F#5: far, nearer, close, alone, then rushing past
